title: Appeal of TE Charles Tarter vs. Evangel Presbytery
disposition_detail: Specifications 2, 3, 4, 5, and 9 were sustained; specifications 1, 6, and 7 were not sustained; specification 8 repeated part of specification 2. The censure was vacated, and the case was remanded for constitutionally compliant proceedings or dismissal.
first_summary: A teaching elder appealed his conviction and deposition for failing to submit to Presbytery. The SJC held that Presbytery’s committee lacked authority to impose several requirements, found due-process and evidentiary defects, vacated the censure, and remanded for further proceedings or dismissal.
summary: A teaching elder appealed his judgment and deposition for refusing Presbytery committee directives and allegedly avoiding accountability. The SJC sustained five of nine specifications, holding that the committee could not impose requirements lacking constitutional warrant or control an independent mission board; vague allegations and testimony unavailable for cross-examination also impaired the trial. Because the record did not prove an ongoing pattern of insubordination, it vacated the censure and remanded for a constitutionally compliant proceeding or dismissal. Three specifications failed, while one duplicated another.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case heading identifies Case 2012-03 and the parties; the full SJC adopted the amended decision (lines 13, 117–119; printed pp. 539, 544).
evidence_notes.dispute: The appeal challenged Presbytery’s approval of its commission’s judgment against Tarter (lines 43–67; printed pp. 540–541).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Specifications 2–5 and 9 were sustained; 1, 6, and 7 failed; 8 duplicated specification 2. The censure was vacated and the matter remanded for compliant process or dismissal (lines 71–115; printed pp. 542–544).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The SJC allowed that a sufficiently detailed indictment and compliant examination might produce a different record; it did not require dismissal (lines 109–115; printed pp. 543–544).
